platform: openSIS: hybrid browser-based SIS with SaaS, GPL Community Edition, licensed on-premises Professional Edition, and role-aware iOS/Android app.

distinctive_features.feature: GPL Community Edition alongside SaaS and licensed on-premises deployment.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Institutions can choose self-hosting, managed cloud, or licensed deployment according to their control and infrastructure needs.

distinctive_features.feature: Staff-based pricing with unlimited student and parent accounts.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Costs are tied to staff accounts rather than the number of students or families using portals.

distinctive_features.feature: Configurable admissions forms with conditional logic, multilingual translation, workflow steps, and applicant-to-student transfer.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Schools can tailor intake processes and carry applicant information into enrolled student records.

distinctive_features.feature: Scheduling for block, rotating, mosaic, year-round, and multi-period models.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: The range supports varied calendars and timetable structures beyond a standard daily schedule.

distinctive_features.feature: Graduation and degree audit with program-linked credit requirements and student progress views.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Institutions can track requirements and show students their progress toward program completion.

distinctive_features.feature: AI tools for lesson plans, report-card comments, natural-language search, and communication translation.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: These tools can assist routine academic and communication tasks within the SIS.

distinctive_features.feature: Copy School templates, year-end rollover, and multi-school enrollment.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: Groups can reuse configurations and manage multiple school records within the platform.

distinctive_features.feature: openIntel data warehousing and business intelligence option.
distinctive_features.why_it_matters: District and enterprise customers can add data visualization and warehousing beyond standard reports.

weaknesses.issue: G2 reviewers report an outdated or less user-friendly interface.
Reviewers report difficulty contacting support and limited support resources.
Reviewers cite limited rules/configuration and application-management functionality.
Reviewers report slow bug fixes and extra effort when changing schedules.
A reviewer alleges discontinued free-account data deletion without effective warning; the allegation conflicts with current terms.
SourceForge users report installation problems and bugs in older Community Edition releases.
Transport, library, hostel, inventory, payroll, alumni, and complete safeguarding modules are not evidenced as native capabilities.
No verified OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, or SIF certification is documented.
Public review volume is very small, with weak ratings reported on G2 and Capterra.

ai_features: AI lesson-plan, curriculum, and syllabus generation
Predictive early-warning insights for academic failure, attendance, enrollment, and course demand
pricing_model_summary: Community Edition is free and GPL-licensed. SaaS plans use staff-based pricing with unlimited student and parent accounts; Professional and enterprise options are quote-based.
biggest_strategic_gap: Broad SIS and scheduling coverage is not matched by native transport, library, hostel, HR/payroll, safeguarding, or verified interoperability standards.
